> Tests?

Tests for the array-based implementation are there, and as these forward to the span-based implementation that's covered.
Explicit span tests are a duplication, but I can add those if you want.
We should add explicit span tests too. Yeah it's duplicative, but that's fine; better to be duplicative than to miss something.

To support all the refactoring described in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45132#issuecomment-763880519 and #43845, we should refactor `SendFileTest` to derive from `SocketTestHelperBase<T>`, similarly to #46862.

I strongly suggest to do it in this PR.

@antonfirsov the refactoring of the tests makes sense, but can this be done in a different PR? I'd like to focus this PR on adding the span-overloads.

And maybe the major reason for my pushback is, that I'm not familiar with `SocketTestHelperBase<T>` and how the things play together, especially as
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f066972c7aa9f9147347623617e789e70aff3d3f/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/tests/FunctionalTests/SendFile.cs#L15 has already a base-class, so this needs to be moved around and I have no clue on how to do this at the moment.
I see #46862 and other code that uses the `SocketTestHelperBase<T>` but this doesn't make it sound for that change. 
Maybe I'm missing a trivial piece of the puzzle now, or we have to do this separately.

@gfoidl `FileCleanupTestBase.GetTestFilePath()` is used to create and auto-cleanup temporary files. The `TempFile` utility is an equivalent tool for this, and it doesn't need subclassing:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/IO/TempFile.cs

`SocketTestHelperBase<T>` is a utility to avoid over-duplicating the same test logic across all the Sync / APM (Begin, End) / SocketAsyncEventArgs / Task test variants. This makes it easier to ensure that the cases which are valid for all those variants are indeed tested for all of them. Using it usually results in better coverage.

What I wanted was to avoid bloating the current `SendFile.cs` further by coding the same tests for the new `Span<byte>` overloads (just to delete them a few weeks later). Nevertheless, if a separate PR is easier for you, I'm fine with that, and I may also take that work after finishing #47229.

Thanks for the explaination!
Please let's sheperd this PR to merge, then do the test stuff where I'd really appreciate

> I'm fine with that, and I may also take that work after finishing #47229.

to see how it's done (and use that knowledge then for the SendFileAsync tests).
I'm fine to defer the `SocketTestHelperBase<T>` work until after we merge this PR, but we should do it before we add the Task-based SendFile overloads.

review_comments: `[PlatformSpecific]` is enough to make this conditional, `[ConditionalTheory]` is used when you need to evaluate `bool` members at runtime.
BTW do we have a test for this? I.e. that trying to do SendFile over UDP throws NotSupportedException? If not we should.

There's a test for https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5a4483eb1c0918542298d1864b7233f962952880/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/tests/FunctionalTests/SendFile.cs#L98

I'll add a test for UDP.
Looks like we don't have test for the `FileNotFoundException` case.

Indeed, that's missing.

As the tests will be refactored, should we file an issue for this and where these points get collected? Or won't we forget about this anyway?

If one of us manages to PR the test refactor within a week, I wouldn't bother with an issue, otherwise it would be wise to start tracking it.

My main fear is that more extensive testing will discover a bunch of corner cases and platform inconsistencies (or even actual bugs) we'll have to deal with. This is what made things hard with my other PR.
Similarly, do we have a test that we get InvalidOperationException if you try to do this with a non blocking socket?

I don't mean ForceNonBlocking. That puts the socket into sync-over-async mode.

I mean literally a nonblocking socket, i.e. socket.Blocking = false.

Tried this too, same result where the above `if` in ValidateBlockingMode won't throw.

![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5755834/105394502-f63e0a00-5c1d-11eb-9049-51b8569d703d.png)

Huh. It seems like we don't actually prevent you from doing a sync SendFile in non-blocking mode.

Does it actually work? What happens if you send a really big file, does it block or return E_WOULDBLOCK or what?

I think we probably should be preventing this, but it looks like we are not currently...
Is that on Linux or Windows?
Windows. Will try Linux soon

On linux it throws:
```
Message: Resource temporarily unavailable
SocketErrorCode: WouldBlock
```

Edit: if set to block, then on linux it runs fine.

Interesting.

We shouldn't block this PR on this issue, since it already exists. I'll file a separate issue.
That's very strange. I'm not surprised it's flaky on Linux, but I am surprised that whether you call "DumpState" or not determines whether it is flaky. Very odd.
Issue here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/47287

Does this handle null values for pre/postBuffer correctly?

Do we have tests for that?

A `null` array will become an empty span, which is checked in the control flow.

No explicit test, but it's covered by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5a4483eb1c0918542298d1864b7233f962952880/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/tests/FunctionalTests/SendFile.cs#L137-L147

I'm not sure what happens when you pin an empty Span. Do you get null? Do you get a valid pointer to some random empty array that actually gets pinned? If the latter, that seems bad

Seems like we should ensure that we pass null to TransmitFile for empty spans.

Just chatted with @stephentoub -- doing (fixed byte* p = someSpan) will indeed give you null if the span is empty.

Would probably be good to assert this too, though.

>  pin an empty Span.

Results in a null-pointer / IntPtr.Zero for this usage after the cast. This is safe.

Didn't see the new comment before writing mine.

The casts https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/878fdf3a3b8f9f8edc65c1177ea4592424c54dc0/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketPal.Windows.cs#L299 make it `IntPtr.Zero` and for the length `0` will be passed to `TransmitFileHelper` where these lengths are checked https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/878fdf3a3b8f9f8edc65c1177ea4592424c54dc0/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketPal.Windows.cs#L1036 so this operation is safe.

I don't understand what should be asserted here.
Yeah, you are right, we are checking the length again in TransmitFileHelper so it doesn't matter either way.

> doing (fixed byte* p = someSpan) will indeed give you null if the span is empty.

Yup.  Just sharing in the name of completeness, that logic lives here:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8c76312b621e2cdb22ca0ee603c5b0e1919134a2/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Span.cs#L255-L262
When you write:
```C#
fixed (byte* p = someSpan)
```
the C# compiler treats that as equivalent to if you wrote:
```C#
fixed (byte* p = &someSpan.GetPinnableReference())
```
thus invoking the previously cited code, which explicitly checks for 0-length and returns null in that case.

Note that this is not the case if you instead used:
```C#
fixed (byte* p = &MemoryMarshal.GetReference(someSpan))
```
whose sole reason to exist is to not perform that 0-length check.
Wouldn't it make sense to also check `SocketException.SocketErrorCode`?
